findings.text: follow-on: the fragment (and the manifest, line 16) states 'All 328 changed float fields are numerical drift', but an independent walk of the old and regenerated receipts finds 326 float leaves that actually changed. The other two are topology_branch.x_point[0] and [1], which are NaN in both receipts and are counted only because nan != nan. The drift conclusion is unaffected; the count overstates the changed population by two.

follow-on: the fragment calls topology_branch.axis[1] 'the lone 0.50 figure', but fixed_point_residual also changes by a large relative amount (1.57e-14 -> 2.72e-14, rel 4.24e-1). Both are floor-level absolute changes and the fragment's table lists fixed_point_residual as 'floor', so the substance holds, but 'lone' does not.

follow-on: the headline bound 2.3e-13 is stated as the maximum over the headline aggregates (ledger totals, plasma current, SOL-over-current fraction), but the common_sol_split totals drift up to 3.6e-13 (common_sol_total_a), slightly more. The stated population matches the check script's own definition, and the overall signed bound (1.6e-10) already dominates, so the conclusion is unaffected; a reader treating the split totals as headline would see a marginally larger figure.

justifications.durability: held down because the guards that matter for this node are not committed. The defect the node answers -- benchmarks/net_current_scaling_census.py::_read_sol_ledger raising ValueError when the receipt lacks clip_mode (line 271) -- has zero committed tests: grep for net_current_scaling_census across tests/ returns nothing, and the only demonstration that the guard fires is the uncommitted run-directory script gate-net-census-read.log. Likewise the repair's own discriminator, check_bound_statement.py, lives only in the run directory and is not committed, so the bound statement is guarded by nothing in the repository. The receipt change itself is partly covered: tests/test_sol_*ledger*_render.py reads the committed receipt and asserts the common_sol_split title match and a 40-hex source_revision (with its own DROP_WALL / DROP_REVISION negative controls), and it passed 4/4 at head, so a corrupted or unstamped receipt would fail it -- but it exercises benchmarks/sol_ledger_current_census, not the _read_sol_ledger guard, and it does not assert the clip_mode key. Two conventional commits with bodies; negative control declared and shown to fail.
justifications.evidence: the corrected claim is true and independently reproducible, but three small record-accuracy blemishes survive. Blemish 1: the fragment and manifest both say '328 changed float fields'; an independent walk finds 326 float leaves that actually changed. The extra two are topology_branch.x_point[0] and [1], which are NaN in BOTH receipts (unchanged) and are counted only because nan != nan in a naive comparison. Blemish 2: the fragment calls topology_branch.axis[1] 'the lone 0.50 figure', but fixed_point_residual also changes by a large relative amount (1.57e-14 -> 2.72e-14, rel 4.24e-1); both are floor-level absolute changes and the table does list fixed_point_residual as 'floor', so the substance holds, but 'lone' is inaccurate. Blemish 3: the fragment states the headline maximum as 2.3e-13 'over the headline aggregates (ledger totals, plasma current, SOL-over-current fraction)', yet the closely-read common_sol_split totals drift slightly more (3.6e-13, common_sol_total_a); the stated population is literally the check's own definition, so the figure is defensible, but a reader who treats the split totals as headline sees a marginally larger number. None of the three changes the conclusion. On the positive side I verified the negative control can fail (the check script reports BOUND-STATEMENT FAIL / exit 1 against the pre-repair fragment and PASS / exit 0 against the repaired one) and that the regenerated receipt is unchanged from c65d983223054fedac666a354cce782e0edb4fc2 (0 render diffs, no key-set change, only the two NaN leaves and identical non-float per-cell fields).
justifications.fit: the repair is a minimal, correctly-scoped prose correction to one fragment; it introduces no code, no new abstraction and no plan/ticket label. The two bounds are stated as a physical population distinction (headline scalars vs per-cell fields), which is the right way to express a floating-point drift bound and matches the idiom of the surrounding evidence table. The census driver, the reader and the receipt are untouched by the repair, so the change cannot perturb the numerical result.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the repair round delivers exactly what the prior finding asked. The evidence fragment (docs/evidence/fragments/forward-solve-api/fsapi-sol-ledger-receipt-regeneration.html:11) now states the two drift bounds by population: the headline aggregates (ledger totals, plasma current, SOL-over-current fraction) change by at most 2.3e-13 relative at ledger.common_sol, and the per-cell current/centroid fields with |value|>1 by at most 1.6e-10 relative at per_cell[111].current_a. I re-derived both figures independently from receipt-before.json (identical to the parent-of-c65d983223054fedac666a354cce782e0edb4fc2 receipt blob, so a genuine pre-regeneration baseline) and the committed receipt, and reproduced 2.260e-13 at /ledger/common_sol and 1.619e-10 at /per_cell[111]/current_a. The manifest (line 16) and the repair commit body (0b205655dc9c67897ab5586a26f587c020ab59a4, 'state the headline and per-cell drift bounds separately') carry the same corrected statement, and the change deliberately leaves the numerical-drift conclusion and the receipt itself untouched, as a prose-only repair should. The overall signed-off bound is now the per-cell 1.6e-10, which is the true maximum over the full changed population of physical quantities.
justifications.scope_discipline: every landed path stays inside the declared write scope. The first commit (c65d983223054fedac666a354cce782e0edb4fc2) touches exactly the sol-ledger-census receipt, its .png/.svg, its render receipt and the evidence fragment; the repair commit (0b205655dc9c67897ab5586a26f587c020ab59a4) touches only the evidence fragment (4 insertions, 3 deletions). No product source or test file outside scope is edited, the shared index, plan and sprint state are untouched, no plan label or ticket identifier appears in a path, symbol or comment, and neither commit message carries AI attribution.
